items.title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease: The NOPARK Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Nicotinamide riboside, a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide precursor, has been proposed as a potential disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson disease based on preclinical and early studies. Whether prolonged oral nicotinamide riboside improves clinical outcomes in Parkinson disease is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether nicotinamide riboside improves clinical outcomes in Parkinson disease compared with placebo.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial conducted at 11 centers in Norway. Eligible participants were patients aged 35 years or older with Parkinson disease diagnosed within 2 years before enrollment, Hoehn and Yahr disease stage less than 3, abnormal dopamine transporter scintigraphy findings confirming dopaminergic nigrostriatal denervation, and stable dopaminergic treatment before enrollment. Of 537 screened individuals, 410 were randomized from May 6, 2020, to June 20, 2024, and 393 were included in the primary analysis. Final follow-up was completed on June 19, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive oral nicotinamide riboside, 500 mg twice daily (n = 206), or matching placebo (n = 204) for 52 weeks.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change from baseline to week 52 in the Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale total score (MDS-UPDRS parts I-III; range, 0-236, with higher scores indicating more severe disease; clinically important differences for improvement and worsening, 6.7 and 5.2 points, respectively), analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures. The 5 key secondary outcomes were the individual parts I, II, and III of the MDS-UPDRS; dopamine transporter single-photon emission computed tomography brain imaging findings; and the Non-Motor Symptoms Scale score (NMSS; range, 0-360, with higher scores indicating greater nonmotor symptom burden).
RESULTS: Among the 393 participants in the primary analysis, the mean age was 65.6 (SD, 9.4) years and 133 (34%) were female. At week 52, the total MDS-UPDRS score increased by 2.45 (95% CI, 0.80-4.10) points with nicotinamide riboside and decreased by 0.27 (95% CI, -1.95 to 1.40) points with placebo, yielding an adjusted mean difference of 2.72 points (95% CI, 0.47-4.98 points; P = .02), favoring placebo. Of the 5 prespecified key secondary outcomes, 4 showed no significant difference, but nonmotor symptom burden worsened more with nicotinamide riboside (NMSS score adjusted mean difference, 4.22 [95% CI, 1.07-7.37] points; P = .009). Serious adverse events occurred in 17 (8.3%) of 205 participants receiving nicotinamide riboside and 29 (14.1%) of 205 receiving placebo in the safety population.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with early Parkinson disease, nicotinamide riboside treatment for 52 weeks did not improve clinical outcomes and was associated with worse clinical outcomes than placebo. These findings do not support nicotinamide riboside as a disease-modifying treatment for Parkinson disease.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03568968.

items.title: Cannabidiol for Severe Behavioral Problems in Youths With Intellectual Disability: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: There is a high level of interest in cannabidiol (CBD) as treatment for severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disabilities. Given the lack of evidence, clinical trials are needed to inform practice.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy of CBD to reduce severe behavioral problems in children and adolescents with intellectual disability.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This parallel design, double-blind placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted between May 11, 2021, and May 8, 2025. Participants were children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years with an intellectual disability and severe behavioral problems from 3 children's hospitals in Australia: The Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, Monash Children's Hospital in Melbourne, and The Children's Hospital Westmead in Sydney.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive CBD isolate in oil (10 mg/kg/d) or placebo orally for 8 weeks, with a 4-week follow-up period.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: The primary outcome was parent-reported score on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist, Irritability (ABC-I) subscale assessed at the end of the 8-week maintenance phase.
RESULTS: Of 131 participants randomized after exclusion of 1 participant randomized in error, 65 were in the CBD group and 66 were in the placebo group. Overall, mean (SD) age was 11.2 (3.1) years, and 98 participants (74.8%) were male. A total of 110 participants (84.0%) had comorbid autism. Primary outcome data were available for 61 participants in the CBD group and 63 in the placebo group. Mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at baseline were 32.2 (7.3) and 30.0 (6.3) in the CBD and placebo groups, respectively. Intention-to-treat analysis showed similar mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at the end of treatment: 21.7 (11.0) in the CBD group and 19.2 (10.7) in the placebo group (mean difference, 2.4; 95% CI, -1.5 to 6.3). A similar proportion of participants experienced at least 1 adverse event in the CBD group (41 [63.1%]) and the placebo group (40 [60.6%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, CBD was not effective in treating severe behavioral problems in youths with intellectual disability. The results suggest that CBD should not be used to treat severe behavioral problems in this population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04821856.

items.title: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy vs Surgery for Stage IA Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a well-established alternative to surgery for nonoperable patients with early-stage non-small cell (NSCLC) lung cancer. However, the role of SBRT in operable patients is unclear as 3 randomized clinical trials comparing SBRT with surgery were closed early because of poor accrual. Existing observational comparisons are limited by confounding because patients who receive SBRT are generally frailer and more comorbid.
OBJECTIVE: To compare cancer-specific mortality between surgery and SBRT using proximal causal inference to adjust for unmeasured confounding due to frailty and comorbidity using proxy variables.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study was a national database analysis of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)-Medicare dataset. Three treatment effect estimates were obtained with increasing control of confounding: unadjusted, standard-regression adjusted for measured confounders as in existing studies, and proximally adjusted for unmeasured confounders. Participants were patients with stage IA NSCLC who underwent sublobar resection or SBRT from 2010 to 2019, followed up through December 21, 2021. Data analysis was performed from April 2023 to August 2026.
EXPOSURES: Sublobar resection vs SBRT. Negative control exposures were constructed from billing codes.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Lung cancer-specific mortality. Negative control outcomes were constructed from other-cause mortality. Results are reported as hazard differences (HD) and 95% CI.
RESULTS: A total of 4251 patients met inclusion and exclusion criteria; 2581 (60.7%) were female and 1670 (39.3%) were male. Their mean (SD) age was 75.6 (6.3) years. A total of 2558 patients underwent SBRT and 1693 underwent surgery. In the unadjusted and covariate-adjusted analyses, SBRT was associated with higher lung cancer cause-specific mortality, HD of 0.047 person-years (95% CI, 0.038-0.055) and 0.024 person-years (95% CI, 0.014-0.034), respectively. However, there was also compelling evidence of confounding due to a strong estimated association with other-cause mortality. In the proximal analysis, other-cause mortality together with negative control exposures were used to indirectly control for hidden confounders, yielding an HD of 0.012 person-years (95% CI, 0.0013-0.027).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study empirically showed that existing observational comparisons of SBRT and surgery are biased because of unmeasured confounding. When proximal causal inference was used to better control for confounding due to frailty and comorbidity, there continued to be a smaller but significant improvement in outcomes associated with surgery, though the effects of residual bias due to differences in pathologic and clinical staging could not be ruled out. This study demonstrates that proximal causal inference can be used to control for unmeasured confounders in a variety of settings.

items.title: Digital Delivery of Apolipoprotein E Genotype and Phosphorylated Tau 217 Results: The eSMARTER Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Patients are increasingly learning Alzheimer disease (AD) genetic and biomarker results through electronic health portals. Evaluation of alternative scalable delivery models for return of AD risk information is needed to best support patient knowledge and psychological well-being.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a digital platform is comparable to clinician-mediated telehealth sessions for returning apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype and plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) results on outcomes of knowledge and psychological well-being.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The Evaluation of Self-Mediated Alternatives for Risk Testing Education and Return of Results (eSMARTER) study was a noninferiority trial of a digital platform compared to clinician-mediated return of APOE genotype and optional p-tau217 results. Enrollment was conducted October 2024 through February 2025. Follow-up was completed November 2025. This was a decentralized, fully remote trial taking place across the contiguous US. Eligible participants were aged 60 to 80 years and had previously undergone APOE genotyping (without disclosure) via GeneMatch, passed psychological screening, had internet access, and could speak English. Of the 13 033 people invited by GeneMatch, 2052 accepted, and 813 were assessed for eligibility. Of 666 randomized, 651 were ultimately included.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized, 2:1, to the eSMARTER digital platform or study clinician-mediated return of APOE genotype. Following the 6-month post-APOE assessment, participants were offered optional p-tau217 disclosure via the same randomized modality.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes at 1 to 7 days following APOE disclosure included changes in anxiety, disease-specific distress, and AD-related knowledge within a priori noninferiority margins.
RESULTS: A total of 674 persons were eligible and provided demographic information. Of these, 651 participants had been randomized to study clinician-mediated (n = 216) or digital disclosure (n = 435) and completed APOE disclosure (mean [SD] age, 68 [4.7] years; 439 [67%] female; mean [SD] telephone Montreal Cognitive Assessment score, 19 [2]; 66 [10%] APOE4 homozygotes, 377 [58%] heterozygotes, and 208 [32%] noncarriers) A total of 604 participants completed the study; 500 completed optional p-tau217 disclosure. Baseline characteristics were balanced across groups. At 1 to 7 days following APOE disclosure, scores on AD-related knowledge, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Anxiety T-score, and disease-specific distress measures met noninferiority.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Return of APOE genotype by the eSMARTER digital platform is noninferior to study clinician-mediated telehealth disclosure. No significant between-group differences were found following return of p-tau217 results. Together, these results suggest that this digital platform may provide an evidence-based scalable approach for returning AD genetic and biomarker results.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06459583.

items.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance to Guide Defibrillator Implantation for LVEF of 36% to 50%: The CMR GUIDE Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Current guidelines do not recommend primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) unless a patient's left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 35% or less. Many sudden cardiac deaths (SCD) occur when LVEF is 36% to 50%. Myocardial scar (a key arrhythmic substrate) can be assessed by late gadolinium enhancement on cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), but robust evidence is lacking regarding a scar-based approach to ICD insertion.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether implantation of ICDs reduces SCD or hemodynamically significant ventricular arrhythmia (HSVA) in patients with an LVEF of 36% to 50% and myocardial scar.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: An open-label randomized clinical trial enrolled adults between 2015 and 2022 who had ischemic or nonischemic cardiomyopathy, an LVEF of 36% to 50%, CMR-defined myocardial scar, and were receiving guideline-directed medical therapy at 18 sites in Australia, Germany, and the UK. Follow-up assessments were completed in 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: A primary prevention ICD (n = 180) vs an implantable loop recorder (ILR) (n = 173).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary composite outcome was SCD or HSVA. Five secondary outcomes were evaluated: SCD, HSVA, heart failure-related hospitalization, cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Of 353 patients randomized (median age, 65 years [IQR, 57-61 years]; 18% female; and 72% had an ischemic etiology), 70% had an LVEF of 40% or greater. The median follow-up was 6.3 years (IQR, 4.8-7.6 years). The primary composite outcome occurred in 14 patients (7.8%) in the ICD group compared with 16 patients (9.2%) in the ILR group (hazard ratio [HR], 0.76 [95% CI, 0.37-1.58]). For the individual components of the primary composite outcome, SCD occurred in 3 patients (1.7%) vs 10 patients (5.8%) in the ILR group (HR, 0.26 [95% CI, 0.07-0.95]) and HSVA occurred in 12 patients (6.7%) vs 6 patients (3.5%), respectively (HR, 1.77 [95% CI, 0.65-4.81]). The rates for all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and heart failure-related hospitalization were similar between groups. In a prespecified analysis of 6 subgroups, the primary outcome occurred less often in patients younger than 70 years in the ICD group (3.3%) vs patients in the ILR group (10.0%) (HR, 0.28 [95% CI, 0.09-0.89]) but not in those aged 70 years or older (16.9% vs 7.5%, respectively) (HR, 2.33 [95% CI, 0.75-7.26]; P = .01 for interaction).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implantation of an ICD did not reduce the composite outcome of SCD or HSVA in patients with an LVEF of 36% to 50% and myocardial scar.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01918215.

items.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in surgically resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (PRIME-HCC): a prospective, phase 1b, single-arm trial and translational analyses.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment.
METHODS: PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population. Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells.
INTERPRETATION: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation.

items.title: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.
DESIGN: Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).
SETTING: Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
PARTICIPANTS: 132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.
LIMITATION: Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.
CONCLUSION: Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Facility for Translational Medicine (Shanghai).

items.title: Absolute Risk of Progression to Cognitive Impairment Based on Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217, Age, Sex, and APOE ε4.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology can be detected years before symptom onset, but some individuals who are biomarker positive and cognitively unimpaired (CU) remain asymptomatic.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate 5- and 10-year absolute risks of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia using continuous plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and p-tau217/amyloid β 42 (Aβ42).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study included participants from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Participants were CU individuals aged 60 to 90 years with baseline Fujirebio Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 measurements, APOE genotyping, and longitudinal clinical follow-up. The MCSA is a population-based longitudinal cohort of residents in Olmsted County, Minnesota; ADNI is a multicenter observational cohort. MCSA data were ascertained from October 2008 to September 2025; ADNI data from September 2005 to January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Age, sex, APOE ε4, p-tau217, and p-tau217/Aβ42.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Transition from CU to MCI and dementia estimated using continuous-time multistate models.
RESULTS: In the MCSA cohort (n = 1644), the median (IQR) age was 72 (66-79) years; 804 participants (49%) were female and 840 (51%) were male. In the ADNI cohort (n = 534), the median (IQR) age was 72 (68-77) years; 297 participants (56%) were female and 237 (44%) were male. A p-tau217 of 0.324 pg/mL vs 0.072 pg/mL (90th vs 10th percentile) was associated with 2.66 (95% CI, 2.02-3.51), 3.02 (95% CI, 2.21-4.12), 2.62 (95% CI, 1.99-3.46), and 2.79 (95% CI, 2.04-3.81) greater hazard of clinical progression in MCSA female participants who did not carry the APOE ε4 variant (ε4-), females who did carry the APOE ε4 variant (ε4+), males who were ε4-, and males who were ε4+, respectively. In ADNI, hazards were 2.67 (95% CI, 1.86-3.85), 2.83 (95% CI, 1.89-4.22), 2.08 (95% CI, 1.48-2.92), and 3.99 (95% CI, 2.59-6.13), respectively. In MCSA, higher baseline p-tau217 and older age were associated with greater absolute risk of progression. At age 75 years and assuming sex and APOE are at the MCSA means of 0.511 and 0.268, 5-year absolute risk of MCI increased from 7% (95% CI, 5%-8%) to 17% (95% CI, 13%-20%) for a p-tau217 concentration of 0.072 vs 0.324 pg/mL; 10-year absolute risk of MCI increased from 15% (95% CI, 12%-18%) to 35% (95% CI, 29%-41%; P < .001 for both). At 0.324 pg/mL, 5-year MCI risk increased from 6% (95% CI, 4%-8%) to 37% (95% CI, 32%-43%) for ages 65 to 85 years; 10-year risks were 17% (95% CI, 12%-21%) and 66% (95% CI, 57%-74%; P < .001 for both). Results were similar for p-tau217/Aβ42.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that higher plasma p-tau217 and older age were associated with higher 5- and 10-year risk of cognitive impairment. Plasma p-tau217 concentrations, combined with age, sex, and APOE ε4 status, can enable individualized estimation of short-term absolute risk of cognitive impairment in CU individuals, with applications in prognosis and trial enrichment in preclinical AD.

items.title: Temporal interference stimulation targeting the ventromedial prefrontal cortex enhances reward learning and improves depression scores.
items.abstract: Reward learning depends on dynamic interactions within frontostriatal circuits that encode reward prediction errors (RPEs). Disruptions in these interactions contribute to neuropsychiatric disorders, yet noninvasive modulation of deep reward circuits remains challenging. Here, we identify frontostriatal neural dynamics underlying reward learning and develop a circuit-targeted neuromodulation approach based on transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS). items.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery.
items.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer's blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

items.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.
METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.
RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death.
CONCLUSIONS: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies.

items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Although metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is traditionally associated with obesity, it is increasingly recognized in individuals with normal weight (ie, lean MASLD).
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical, histologic, and prognostic features of lean MASLD, and evaluate the performance of noninvasive tests for advanced fibrosis.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multinational, retrospective observational study of adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD from 41 countries from the Global MASLD project.
EXPOSURES: Lean vs overweight/obese MASLD, defined by body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and clinical events (hepatocellular carcinoma, hepatic decompensation, liver transplant, death), intermediate outcomes included histologic fibrosis severity, and tests included the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by transient elastography.
RESULTS: Among 18 326 patients (mean [SD] age, 50.9 [13.1] years; 8714 [47.6%] male), 6.7% were lean by BMI. Among 12 202 patients with waist circumference available, 6.0% were lean by waist circumference (κ = 0.41). Lean MASLD was most prevalent in Asia (11.3% by BMI, 11.7% by waist circumference). Compared with overweight/obese MASLD, lean MASLD had lower prevalence of type 2 diabetes (38.2% vs 48.3%; difference, -10.2% [95% CI, -13.0% to -7.4%]), advanced fibrosis (29.3% vs 37.2%; difference, -7.8% [95% CI, -10.5% to -5.2%]), and Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Scores (mean [SD], 3.96 [1.81] vs 4.41 [1.68]; difference, -0.44 [95% CI, -0.56 to -0.33]). The FIB-4 demonstrated lower accuracy for predicting advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) in lean vs overweight/obese MASLD (area under the curve, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.73-0.79] vs 0.79 [95% CI, 0.78-0.80]; difference, -0.03 [95% CI, -0.06 to 0.00]), while LSM had higher accuracy (area under the curve, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.84-0.90] vs 0.83 [95% CI, 0.82-0.84]; difference, 0.04 [95% CI, 0.01-0.07]). Unadjusted rates per 100 person-years in lean vs overweight/obese MASLD were 1.08 vs 0.91 for all-cause mortality and 1.51 vs 1.43 for clinical events, respectively; lean status was not independently associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.90 [95% CI, 0.69-1.16]) or clinical events (aHR, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.76-1.17]). Advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) was associated with all-cause mortality (1.46 vs 0.77 per 100 person-years; aHR, 2.10 [95% CI, 1.71-2.57]) and clinical events (3.21 vs 0.89 per 100 person-years; aHR, 3.41 [95% CI, 2.90-4.03]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Lean MASLD represents a distinct phenotype with milder histologic disease but similar clinical outcomes compared with overweight/obese MASLD. Fibrosis severity, rather than body composition, was associated with prognosis and LSM was reliable in lean individuals.

items.title: Genome-directed treatment targets and mutational signature biomarkers: a retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical application of precision oncology therapies is currently restricted to selected cancer cases harbouring highly specific mutations. Targeted therapies are typically approved for use in specific tumour types in which these alterations occur frequently. We aimed to systematically catalogue targetable alterations and genome-wide biomarkers across all solid tumour types to identify additional therapeutic opportunities.
METHODS: In this retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis, for the primary cancer cohort, we used matched fresh frozen tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a discovery cohort of 11 013 tumours comprising 19 tumour types collected from 10 334 participants in the UK-based 100 000 Genomes Project (100kGP). Participants were recruited to this cohort through 13 National Health Service Genomic Medicine Centres or hospitals affiliated to the 100kGP between 2012 and 2019. For the metastatic cancer cohort, we used matched tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a cohort of 6016 solid tumours collected from 5658 patients from the Netherlands who contributed to the Hartwig Medical Foundation (HMF) database (accessed Aug 19, 2025). Snap-frozen tumour DNA and matched normal DNA from blood samples underwent whole-genome sequencing. Potentially targetable alterations, comprising (1) immediately actionable alterations, (2) investigational alterations, and (3) mutational signature-informed features, were sought in all samples. The primary outcome of this study was to assess the pan-cancer frequency and tissue distribution of potentially targetable alterations.
FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2025, and March 3, 2026, we analysed samples from 17 029 tumours from the 100kGP and HMF cohorts. Immediately actionable alterations were identified in 2081 (18·9%) of 11 013 primary and 1559 (25·9%) of 6016 metastatic cancers; a further 1204 (10·9%) primary and 867 (14·4%) metastatic cancers harboured investigational alterations or mutational signature-informed features. 2914 (51·1%) of the 5706 immediately actionable variants identified were found in tumour types where the biomarker is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Although some immediately actionable alterations (including gene-fusion targets and MET exon 14 skipping variants) were restricted to fewer tumour types, most immediately actionable alterations (including HER2 amplification, RAS-RAF pathway alterations, IDH1 mutations, and DNA repair deficiencies) occurred across multiple tumour types, frequently beyond those for which matched targeted therapies are currently approved. Mutational-signature biomarkers of DNA repair or replication deficiencies were similarly observed across tumour types. Metastatic cancers, including rare and moderately rare tumour types and cancers of unknown primary, harboured a notably high prevalence and diversity of targetable events.
INTERPRETATION: Our findings support comprehensive whole-genome sequencing assessment of cancers irrespective of tumour type. Prospective clinical trials are required to establish whether therapeutic vulnerabilities identified by whole-genome sequencing can extend the effective use of targeted therapies beyond their current tumour-specific indications.
